items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: John and I had some very meaningful talks on occasion... we had a great deal of admiration and respect for each other.

ctx.x: So this is why I feel that -- and then, of course, the man who was so great at Columbia Records, whom I didn't mention earlier because I was only concerned with really the pop department, the man, Goddard Lieberson, who was head of the serious department and so on, and a very artistic man and a man who really treated the whole music thing with dignity. I'm glad I had the good fortune to be associated with some of these people. John Hammond was there, who really wasn't into our band because we were a little too…
would still be enthusiastic about for everything we did. And if you've ever had the feeling of having a company behind (unintelligible), you, we did. That was very important in those days.
